Author: D Khandro
Original_Text: Below par and blaséI went to Apple store in Regent St, London on Sat 11 April 2026.When I entered the store there were 3 greeting staff. I passed by one of them because he was engrossed on his phone and not in the least bit interested in who was coming in. (When I was waiting a bit later, I noticed he never once looked up; he had no interest whatsoever in his job.)The other 2 greeters were in a conversation. I decided to butt in and asked to see someone. They said you can just look around. I said No, I came to buy a phone and wanted someone to show me what was available. I was coming from  Adroid.So they put my name down and told me to wait under a tree.Eventually, AK came. He was the only person that I met who was knowledgeable, cosiderate and astute.When I had chosen my phone, I went upstairs to transfer data to the new phone.1. The man forgot to turn on the wifi and bluetooth.2. He said 9 times out of 10 the transfer fails.3. He said the shop wifi was inadequate.4. As we could not access the cloud, I had to leave with a non- functioning phone - no email, no whatsapp and I don't know what else because I kept getting a message saying - complete set up.Now I'm trying to use my old phone on unsecure wifi because the sim is in the new iphone.I'm carrying useless lead weight around with me.Another issue:I decided to buy a cover. I chose the green one but they didn't  have one. The other store didn't have any either. They tried to get me to choose another colour but I was not going to pay £50 for a cover I did not like.I thought Apple would at least have functional technology, if not the wizardry it proclaims from its advertising.They can't even keep a stock check.Fortunately, I found a cover in a local phone shop for £8.

Author: Grim Ghoul
Original_Text: You’ve introduced age verification, and let’s be clear, this looks like a stepping stone toward digital ID.I’ve been a loyal customer for years. I’ve owned:iPhone 13 Pro MaxiPhone 14 Pro MaxiPhone 15 Pro MaxiPhone 16 Pro MaxiPhone 17 Pro MaxBut this is where I draw the line.Governments in countries like the UK and Australia have already pushed for stronger identity systems online, and faced resistance. Now it feels like those same ideas are being introduced indirectly through platforms like Apple Inc..Age verification might sound harmless on the surface, but it opens the door to something much bigger:Increased identity checksReduced anonymity onlineGradual normalisation of digital ID systemsUsing “protecting children” as the justification doesn’t make this risk disappear. Policies like this have a history of expanding beyond their original purpose.This isn’t about politics, it’s about control, privacy, and the direction technology is heading.Because of this change, I won’t be using Apple products going forward.

Author: Beck W.
Original_Text: I’ve been subscribed to YouTube Premium through Apple for over 3 years, paying £16.99/month for a service that actually costs £12.99 when purchased directly online — something that was never clearly disclosed.Over that time, I was overcharged by £146 for absolutely no difference in the service provided.As soon as I realised, I cancelled and switched to paying the correct price.
